content.title: About
content.content: Gluten‑free toasted bread is a ready‑to‑eat product made from gluten‑free grains such as rice, corn, buckwheat and others, then toasted to a golden crust. It has a crunchy texture, a light toasted aroma, and is suitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Gluten‑free breads often contain seeds, nuts or dried fruit to boost flavor and nutrition.
Toasting enhances aroma and creates a crisp crust while reducing moisture, which extends shelf life.
Unlike traditional wheat bread, gluten‑free bread lacks gluten, so its crumb can be denser.
Many gluten‑free mixes are fortified with B‑vitamins and iron to offset possible deficiencies in a gluten‑free diet.
Toasted gluten‑free bread is frequently used for sandwiches, croutons and as a base for various dishes.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Gluten‑free grains like buckwheat and quinoa provide dietary fiber that supports healthy digestion.

items.title: Moderate glycemic index
items.content: Toasting slightly lowers the glycemic index, making the bread more suitable for blood‑sugar control.

items.title: Source of vitamins and minerals
items.content: Fortified gluten‑free mixes often contain iron, folate and B‑vitamins important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Gluten‑free
items.content: Safe for individuals with celiac disease, gluten sensitivity, or those following a gluten‑free diet.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Added seeds such as sunflower or pumpkin are rich in vitamin E and polyphenols.

items.title: Allergy to specific ingredients
items.content: The bread may contain nuts, seeds or soy protein, which can trigger allergic reactions.

items.title: Calorie density
items.content: Toasted bread can be higher in fats and calories than its fresh counterpart.

items.title: Additive content
items.content: Some manufacturers use preservatives and flavor enhancers that may be undesirable for sensitive individuals.

items.title: Nutrient loss over time
items.content: Prolonged storage can lead to fat oxidation and loss of vitamins.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Gluten‑free toasted bread can be enjoyed as a snack, used for croutons, sandwiches, soup toppings, or as a base for casseroles. It pairs well with butter, avocado, hummus or low‑fat cheese.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the bread in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. For longer storage keep it in the refrigerator or freezer to maintain the crisp crust and prevent mold growth.
